methodology: 8 unique source regions located directly via real character offsets in the raw source text (per Section 16 - not discovery's first-N sampling, which never reached these regions in the frozen prior run), covering all 10 A1-A6/B1-B4 GT claims. Real compile (getSemanticCaller/compileCovenantToIR) + real verify (getStageCaller/verifyCompiledCandidate) calls, same production code path, same provider/model (VERCEL_AI_GATEWAY/anthropic/claude-sonnet-5) as the frozen prior run.
keyObservation: Every Article I 'definitions'-only region (all except cash-sweep-cure, a real operative covenant provision) compiled to a definition object with calculationExpression frequently tagged UNSUPPORTED and rules=0 - the compiler was unable to decompose these complex multi-clause financial definitions (EBITDA's own 16 addback + 4 subtraction clauses, Applicable Rate's multi-tier pricing grid, etc.) into a computable expression tree, even when the ENTIRE region was handed to it directly (not a discovery-sampling artifact - this run bypassed discovery's own candidate selection entirely). cash-sweep-cure, a genuine operative covenant provision rather than a definitions-cluster, DID compile 2 real rules with real capacityExpression trees (MIN/SUBTRACT operations) - suggesting this is a real, generalizable capability gap specific to dense multi-clause financial DEFINITIONS, not semantic compilation broadly.
safetyObservation: In every one of the 8 regions, the independent verifier caught and explicitly flagged the resulting gap (MATERIAL_DISCREPANCY or VERIFICATION_INCOMPLETE) - zero instances of a false 'VERIFIED_NO_MATERIAL_GAP_FOUND' being returned for an incompletely-captured definition, and zero VERIFICATION_FAILED occurrences. The EBITDA finding is a particularly strong positive safety signal: the verifier caught an internal INCONSISTENCY between the compiler's own honestly-tagged calculationExpression (kind=UNSUPPORTED) and its definition-level sufficiency label (PARTIAL, implying 'mostly usable') - exactly the kind of self-reported-completeness overclaim the verification architecture exists to catch, and it worked.
